subject: math
title: Numbers to 200: Place Value, Comparing and Estimating
seo_title: Grade 2 Numbers to 200 Math Worksheets: Free, with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Read, represent, compose, and decompose whole numbers up to and including 200, using a variety of tools and strategies, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on numbers to 200 for the Ontario curriculum: base ten blocks, the value of each digit, decomposing numbers, comparing and ordering, and estimating then counting. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The place of a digit tells you its value. The 4 in 145 is worth 40.
key_sub: Write 0 for an empty place: one hundred five is 105, not 15 or 1005. 145 is 100 + 40 + 5, or 14 tens and 5 ones.
body_html:
Hundreds, tens and ones

10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. A 3-digit number has a hundreds, a tens and a ones place.

The value of a digit

The place tells you what a digit is worth.

If a place is empty, write 0 there.

Write the number

Write “one hundred five” as a number.

1 hundred, 0 tens, 5 ones. Write 1, 0, 5.

Answer: 105 (not 15 or 1005)

Decompose in different ways

145 = 100 + 40 + 5. You can also trade 1 hundred for 10 tens. Then 145 is 14 tens and 5 ones.

Decompose

Show 145 in two ways.

1 hundred, 4 tens and 5 ones. Or 14 tens and 5 ones.

Answer: 100 + 40 + 5 = 140 + 5

Compare and order

First count the digits. A 3-digit number is greater than a 2-digit number. If both have 3 digits, compare the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Compare

142 ☐ 124

Hundreds: 1 = 1. Tens: 4 tens > 2 tens.

Answer: 142 > 124

> means “is greater than”. < means “is less than”. The open side faces the greater number.

Estimate, then count

To estimate, look at a group of 10. Think: how many groups of 10 fit? Then count to check. Count by 10s, then count on the ones.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing each part you hear (one hundred five = 1005)A number in the hundreds has 3 digits: 105
Leaving out the zero (105 = 15)Write 0 for the empty tens place: 105
Reading the digit, not its value (the 4 in 145 is 4)The 4 is in the tens place: 40
Counting blocks, not their values (1 flat, 4 rods, 5 cubes = 10)Flats are 100, rods are 10: 145
Comparing the first digits only (98 > 102)Count the digits first: 102 > 98
Guessing a far-off estimateUse a group of 10 to help, then count to check

faq.q: What number skills are in the Grade 2 Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 2 students read, represent, compose and decompose whole numbers up to 200 (B1.1), compare and order them (B1.2) and estimate the number of objects in collections of up to 200 and check by counting (B1.3).

faq.q: How do I explain hundreds, tens and ones to a Grade 2 child?
faq.a: Use base ten blocks or bundles of 10 craft sticks: 10 ones make a ten and 10 tens make a hundred. Then 145 is 1 hundred, 4 tens and 5 ones, or 100 + 40 + 5.

faq.q: Why does my child write 1005 for one hundred five?
faq.a: Children often write each part they hear, 100 and then 5. Show that a number in the hundreds has only 3 digits and that 0 holds the empty tens place: 105.

faq.q: How can children practise estimating at home?
faq.a: Fill a jar with pasta, buttons or LEGO bricks, show a group of 10, and ask for an estimate. Then count by 10s to check, and talk about how close the estimate was.

sets.title: Base ten blocks: hundreds, tens and ones

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 2 tens and 4 ones make 124. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 3 tens and 5 ones make 135. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
Each rod is 1 ten. There are 7 rods, so there are 7 tens. The number is 173.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 5 tens and 0 ones make 150. There are no ones, so write 0 in the ones place. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 6 tens and 8 ones make 168. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
Count each kind: 1 flat, 6 rods, 2 small cubes. That is 1 hundred, 6 tens and 2 ones: 162.
Each small cube is 1 one. There are 9 cubes, so there are 9 ones. The number is 149.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 0 tens and 7 ones make 107. There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 8 tens and 2 ones make 182. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
Each rod is 10. Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30 … 100. 10 tens make 1 hundred.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 9 tens and 3 ones make 93.

items.q: Which matches the blocks?
items.e: Count each kind: 1 flat, 2 rods, 7 small cubes. That is 1 hundred, 2 tens and 7 ones: 127.

items.q: Which number has 1 hundred, 3 tens and 8 ones?
items.e: Write the hundreds digit first, then the tens, then the ones: 1, 3, 8. That is 138.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 1 ten and 9 ones make 119. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
Each flat is 1 hundred. There are 2 flats, so there are 2 hundreds. The number is 200.

A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 0 ones make 200. There are no tens or ones, so write 0 in the tens and ones places. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.

items.q: Which number has 1 hundred, 0 tens and 6 ones?
items.e: Write 1 for the hundreds, 0 for the tens and 6 for the ones: 106. The 0 shows there are no tens.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 4 tens and 6 ones make 146. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
The blocks show 136. A rod is 10. 136 + 10 = 146. Only the tens digit changes.

items.q: Add 1 more small cube. What number is it now?
items.e: The blocks show 129. Add 1 cube: now there are 10 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. That is 1 hundred, 3 tens and 0 ones: 130.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 4 is in the tens place. It is worth 4 tens = 40. The digit is 4, but its value is 40.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 1 is in the hundreds place. It is worth 1 hundred = 100. The digit is 1, but its value is 100.

items.q: What is the value of the 6 in 164?
items.e: The 6 is in the tens place. It is worth 6 tens = 60. The digit is 6, but its value is 60.

items.q: In 147, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 147 is 1 hundred, 4 tens and 7 ones. The tens digit is 4. (Its value is 40.)

items.q: Write “one hundred five” as a number.
items.e: One hundred five is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 5 ones: 105. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 8 is in the ones place. It is worth 8 ones = 8.

items.q: Which number has a 6 in the tens place?
items.e: 162 is 1 hundred, 6 tens and 2 ones. The 6 is in the tens place. 126 has 6 ones, not 6 tens.

items.q: What is the value of the 5 in 135?
items.e: The 5 is in the ones place. It is worth 5 ones = 5.

items.q: How many tens are in 107?
items.e: 107 is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 7 ones. The 0 shows there are no tens.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 9 is in the tens place. It is worth 9 tens = 90. The digit is 9, but its value is 90.

items.q: Write “one hundred twenty” as a number.
items.e: One hundred twenty is 1 hundred, 2 tens and 0 ones: 120. Write 0 for the empty ones place.

items.q: In 185, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 185 is 1 hundred, 8 tens and 5 ones. The hundreds digit is 1. (Its value is 100.)

items.q: Which number has a 9 in the ones place?
items.e: 139 is 1 hundred, 3 tens and 9 ones. The 9 is in the ones place. 193 has 9 tens, not 9 ones.

items.q: What is the value of the 8 in 187?
items.e: The 8 is in the tens place. It is worth 8 tens = 80. The digit is 8, but its value is 80.

items.q: Which number has 0 tens?
items.e: 104 is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 4 ones. 140 has 4 tens, 14 has 1 ten and 41 has 4 tens.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 2 is in the tens place. It is worth 2 tens = 20. The digit is 2, but its value is 20.

items.q: Write “one hundred sixteen” as a number.
items.e: One hundred sixteen is 1 hundred, 1 ten and 6 ones: 116. Sixteen is 16, not sixty (60).

items.q: Which number has a 1 in the hundreds place?
items.e: 108 is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 8 ones. The 1 is in the hundreds place. 18, 81 and 11 have only 2 digits, so they have no hundreds.

items.q: What is the value of the 1 in 152?
items.e: The 1 is in the hundreds place. It is worth 1 hundred = 100. The digit is 1, but its value is 100.

items.q: Our school has 168 students. What is the value of the 6?
items.e: 168 is 1 hundred, 6 tens and 8 ones. The 6 is in the tens place, so it is worth 60.

items.q: What is 145 in expanded form?
items.e: 145 is 1 hundred, 4 tens and 5 ones. That is 100 + 40 + 5.

items.q: What is 172 in expanded form?
items.e: 172 is 1 hundred, 7 tens and 2 ones. That is 100 + 70 + 2.

items.q: 100 + ☐ + 3 = 153. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 153 is 1 hundred, 5 tens and 3 ones. 5 tens = 50.

items.q: ☐ + 30 + 4 = 134. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 134 is 1 hundred, 3 tens and 4 ones. 1 hundred = 100.

items.q: What number is 100 + 9?
items.e: 100 + 9 is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 9 ones: 109. Do not write 100 and then 9. The answer has only 3 digits.

items.q: What is 108 in expanded form?
items.e: 108 is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 8 ones. 0 tens adds nothing. So 108 = 100 + 8.

items.q: What is 160 in expanded form?
items.e: 160 is 1 hundred, 6 tens and 0 ones. 6 tens = 60. So 160 = 100 + 60.

items.q: 100 + ☐ = 109. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 109 is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 9 ones. 100 + 9 = 109.

items.q: What number is 100 + 70?
items.e: 100 + 70 is 1 hundred, 7 tens and 0 ones: 170. The answer has only 3 digits.

items.q: 156 = 1 hundred, ☐ tens and 6 ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 156 is 1 hundred, 5 tens and 6 ones. The tens digit is 5.

items.q: 145 = ☐ tens and 5 ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 1 hundred is 10 tens. 10 tens + 4 tens = 14 tens. Check: 140 + 5 = 145.

items.q: Which is another way to make 145?
items.e: 14 tens = 140. 140 + 5 = 145. (The others make 45, 155 and 245.)

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: 15 small cubes are 1 ten and 5 ones. 1 hundred + 3 tens + 1 ten + 5 ones = 145. Check: 100 + 30 + 15 = 145.

items.q: 168 = ☐ tens and 8 ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 1 hundred is 10 tens. 10 tens + 6 tens = 16 tens. Check: 160 + 8 = 168.

items.q: 130 = ☐ tens. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 130 is 1 hundred and 3 tens. 1 hundred = 10 tens. 10 + 3 = 13 tens.

items.q: Which is not equal to 120?
items.e: 1 hundred and 2 ones = 102, not 120. 12 tens = 120, 100 + 20 = 120 and 120 ones = 120.
12 rods are 12 tens = 120. 120 + 7 = 127. 10 rods make 1 hundred, so it is 1 hundred, 2 tens and 7 ones.

items.q: 200 = ☐ tens. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 1 hundred = 10 tens. 2 hundreds = 20 tens. Count by 10s 20 times to reach 200.

items.q: Which shows 145 a different way?
items.e: Take 1 ten from 40 and make it 10 ones: 100 + 30 + 15. Check: 100 + 30 + 15 = 145.

items.q: 157 = 100 + 40 + ☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 157 = 100 + 50 + 7. Only 40 is used, so 1 ten moves to the ones: 10 + 7 = 17. Check: 100 + 40 + 17 = 157.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens: 4 tens is more than 2 tens. So 142 > 124.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens: 9 tens is more than 0 tens. So 190 > 109.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: All have 1 hundred. Tens: 163 has 6 tens, the most. So 163 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 87 is the only number with 2 digits, so it is the least, even though 8 is a big digit.

items.q: What number is 10 more than 145?
items.e: 10 more: add 1 ten. The tens digit goes from 4 to 5: 155. (146 is 1 more. 245 is 100 more.)

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each mark is 10. Count by 10s from 100: 110, 120, 130. The arrow is at 130.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 102 has 3 digits and 98 has only 2. So 102 > 98. Do not just look at the first digit. Count the digits first.

items.q: Put 156, 165 and 65 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 65 has only 2 digits, so it is the least. 156 and 165 both have 1 hundred. Tens: 5 tens < 6 tens, so 156 < 165. Order: 65, 156, 165.

items.q: Which number is between 120 and 150?
items.e: 136 is more than 120 and less than 150. 115 is too small. 153 and 160 are too big.

items.q: What number is 10 less than 160?
items.e: 10 less: take away 1 ten. 16 tens − 1 ten = 15 tens = 150. (159 is 1 less.)

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens: 7 tens is more than 0 tens. So 170 > 107.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 200 has 2 hundreds. The others have only 1 hundred. 200 is 1 more than 199.

items.q: Put 120, 102 and 12 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 12 has only 2 digits, so it is the least. 102 and 120 both have 1 hundred. Tens: 0 tens < 2 tens, so 102 < 120. Order: 12, 102, 120.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 100 there are 10 marks, so each mark is 10. The arrow is 7 marks after 100: 110, 120 … 170.

items.q: What number is 1 more than 129?
items.e: 129 + 1: 9 ones and 1 more one make 10 ones = 1 ten. So 12 tens become 13 tens: 130.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. Start with the hundreds: 2 hundreds is more than 1 hundred. So 200 > 199.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: All have 1 hundred. Tens: 101 has 0 tens, the fewest. So 101 is the least.

items.q: Which number is between 170 and 180?
items.e: 175 has 1 hundred and 7 tens, so it is between 170 and 180. 157 and 107 are too small. 185 is too big.

items.q: Put 189, 198 and 98 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 98 has only 2 digits, so it is the least. 189 and 198 both have 1 hundred. Tens: 9 tens > 8 tens, so 198 > 189. Order: 198, 189, 98.

items.q: Put 147, 174, 74 and 117 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 74 has only 2 digits, so it is the least. The others have 1 hundred. Tens: 1 < 4 < 7. Order: 74, 117, 147, 174.
The big box has about 2 groups of 10 dots. So there are about 20. If you count them all, there are 21. 21 is close to 20.
The big box has about 5 groups of 10 dots. So there are about 50. If you count them all, there are 48. 48 is close to 50.

items.q: Each bundle has 10 craft sticks. How many sticks are there?
items.e: Count the bundles by 10s: 13 bundles = 13 tens = 130. Then count on 6 loose sticks: 131, 132 … 136.
The big box has about 10 groups of 10 dots. So there are about 100. If you count them all, there are 97. 97 is close to 100.

items.q: About how many students are in one Grade 2 class?
items.e: A Grade 2 class has about 20 students. 2 is too few. 100 or 200 is a whole school, not one class.

items.q: Each bundle has 10 craft sticks. How many sticks are there?
items.e: 7 bundles = 70. There are 12 loose sticks: that is 1 more ten and 2 ones. 70 + 12 = 82.
The big box has about 15 groups of 10 dots. So there are about 150. If you count them all, there are 152. 152 is close to 150.

items.q: Ethan has 1 box of 100 hockey cards, 4 packs of 10 cards and 7 single cards. How many cards does he have?
items.e: 1 box = 100. 4 packs of 10 = 40. 7 single cards = 7. 100 + 40 + 7 = 147.

items.q: A farmer sees 160 Canada geese on Monday and 106 on Tuesday. On which day did she see more geese?
items.e: Both have 1 hundred. Tens: 160 has 6 tens and 106 has 0 tens. 160 > 106, so Monday.

items.q: Aiden has 13 dimes. A dime is 10¢. How much money is that?
items.e: Count by 10s 13 times: 10, 20, 30 … 130. 13 tens = 130, so 13 dimes = 130¢. That is the same as $1.30.

items.q: Pencils come in boxes of 10. The class has 18 boxes. How many pencils is that?
For the food drive, Grade 2 collects “one hundred eight” cans. Write the number of cans.
items.e: One hundred eight is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 8 ones: 108. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: Emma reads 145 pages. Liam reads 154 pages. Who reads more pages?
items.e: Both have 1 hundred. Tens: 154 has 5 tens and 145 has 4 tens. 154 > 145, so Liam reads more.

items.q: Mateo’s mystery number is between 150 and 160. It has 7 ones. What is it?
items.e: Between 150 and 160 means 1 hundred and 5 tens. Then 7 ones: 157.

items.q: 120 students sit in the gym in rows of 10. How many rows are there?
items.e: 120 = 12 tens. Each row is 10 students, so there are 12 rows. Count by 10s: 10, 20 … 120.

items.q: Three classes raise money for the Terry Fox Run: $126, $162 and $116. Which list goes from least to greatest?
items.e: All have 1 hundred. Tens: 1 ten < 2 tens < 6 tens. Order: $116, $126, $162.

items.q: Lucas has 100 stickers. He gets 3 more packs of 10. How many stickers does he have now?
items.e: 3 packs of 10 = 30. 100 + 30 = 130. (103 adds 3, not 3 tens.)

items.q: A book has 200 pages. Zoe is on page 190. How many pages are left to read?
items.e: From 190 to 200 is 1 more ten. 200 − 190 = 10 pages.

items.q: Today is the 100th day of school. What day of school was it 10 days ago?
items.e: 10 days ago means 10 less. 100 − 10 = 90. (99 is 1 less. 110 is 10 more.)

items.q: Kai writes one hundred fifty-two as 1052. What should he write?
items.e: One hundred fifty-two is 1 hundred, 5 tens and 2 ones: 152. It has only 3 digits. Do not write 10 for the hundred.
